- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (sentiment > 0.2) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (sentiment < 0.1) — model is overly optimistic.
- Lag in correction: model often fails to adjust downward after a spike, delaying mean reversion.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and underweights lows, leading to persistent overconfidence in upward trends.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly sensitive to short-term sentiment shifts, not long-term trend persistence.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings), model reacts too aggressively — overcorrects or undercorrects.
- Avoid extrapolating recent sentiment trends into future prices without confirming momentum reversal.
